L34@P0-1: For assistance in using Records Online, contact the City Clerk DepartmentTips and Instructions for More Effective Searches
L35@P1: To narrow your search to a certain type of document (recommended), use the drop down menu
L36@P1: under Search Type to choose the document type for the document you wish to locate
L37@P1: (ordinance, contracts, etc.).
L38@P1: If you do not know the document type, or you wish to search for a certain name or term across
L39@P1: all types of documents, use the “All Records Query.”
L40@P1: There are two types of search functions for each document type –Full Text Queries and
L41@P1: Keyword Queries.
L42@P1: A "full text" query locates a specified search term in the record. For example, if you wanted to
L43@P1: search the documents for the term “dog park” or “plant based” or “sidewalks” you would use the
L44@P1: full text query.
L45@P1: A "keywords" query searches in the data fields associated with the document type you select.
L46@P1: A keywords search does not search the text of the document. The keyword queries have
L47@P1-2: different data fields assigned depending on the document type. Examples of data fields include Document Date, Document Number (resolutions and ordinances), or Document Source (a
L48@P2: department, commission, or elected official).
L49@P2: For all date fields in all query types, the proper search format is mm/dd/yyyy.
L50@P2: Full Text Queries
L51@P2: In a full text query, you can combine your search terms with other data fields. This will help
L52@P2: narrow your search. For example, if you want to search for “dog park” but only within a certain
L53@P2: timeframe you can use the full text query and enter your desired date range.
L54@P2: For full-text queries, you may use the following text search tools:
L55@P2: Exact Phrase: "term1 term2"
L56@P2: Definition: Simple text search for a specific phrase of consecutive words
L57@P2: Example: “paving plan” “civic center” “Berkeley marina”
L58@P2: Boolean: term1 AND term2 OR term3 NOT term4
L59@P2: Definition: Provides options to search for non-consecutive words and/or exclude certain words
L60@P2: Example: “bicycle AND plan NOT pedestrian”
L61@P2: Soundex: S{term}
L62@P2: Definition: An algorithm used to search for alternate spellings of a name, using the way the
L63@P2: name is pronounced instead of the way it is spelled.
L64@P2: Example: “S{Humfree}” when searching for “Humphrey”
L65@P2: Fuzzy: F{term}
L66@P2: Definition: A fuzzy search applies search algorithms in a more lenient way than hard search
L67@P2: algorithms that only match specific and rigid results.
L68@P2: Example: In a rigid search, a user may enter a word like “animal.” While the rigid search will only
L69@P2: look for instances of “animal,” a fuzzy search will add the plural form, “animals,” or other similar
L70@P2: search terms, or may look for results that have been misspelled or differently punctuated.
L71@P2: Near: N#{term1, term2}
L72@P2: Definition: Searches for two words that are non-consecutive, but in the document or record. In
L73@P2: your search, the number value that you enter in place of the “#” sign determines how many
L74@P2: words in each direction are between the two terms, i.e. how far do you want the algorithm to
L75@P2: look for the second term.
